units.title: Forecast: wind increasing, rain this evening
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound, issued 06:00 ST. Today: southwesterly 4 or 5, increasing 6 later in the west. Cloud thickening from the west by afternoon, with rain reaching the outer islands this evening. Sea moderate, becoming rough later. A swell of 1.5 to 2 m on exposed east and south coasts by tomorrow. Max 8 C. Outlook: a yellow wind warning is likely for tomorrow. Small craft should plan for deteriorating conditions.

units.title: Kittering Holm: our role
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. The Coastguard has asked whether our relief vessel could support a daylight transfer from Kittering Holm. The vessel is completing a refit at Weyhaven and is not yet in service. We have said we will help if it can be done safely. No sailing has been scheduled. Timetabled services are unaffected this morning; afternoon sailings may be disrupted by the weather, so please check this page.

units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard Marrow Sound. Update to the notice regarding Kittering Holm. The beacon remains active. A vessel-based response in daylight is being planned with partner agencies; no date has been fixed, and it will depend on conditions at the island's east dock. No further information can be given about persons on the island. Mariners: keep at least one nautical mile from the Holm and do not approach after dark. Sightings of lights should be reported, not investigated.

units.title: Kittering Holm: statement and information point
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. The council is not a party to the private contract on Kittering Holm and holds no information about personnel. Gilliver Village Hall will be open from 10:00 to 20:00 each day this week as an information point, staffed by volunteers, with tea, a telephone and the latest Coastguard notices. Normal council services, including bin collections, continue.

units.title: Grieve: Holm contract 'concluded'; no word on crew
units.author: courier
units.text: Grieve Land Services has issued a short written statement about Kittering Holm. It says the contract 'has concluded in accordance with its terms' and that 'all site personnel were advised of the arrangements applying at conclusion'. It does not say what those arrangements were, or whether anyone remains on the island.

units.author: courier
units.text: Asked by the Courier whether its workers had been brought back to the mainland, a Grieve spokesperson said the company 'would not comment on individual employment matters'. Asked whether it had any vessel available to send, the spokesperson referred the Courier to the Coastguard and ended the call.

units.author: courier
units.text: Ardent Vale Holdings, which bought the Holm through an intermediary last year, has not responded to six requests for comment since yesterday morning. Its community information email address sends no reply. A receptionist at its office in Halvard described the office as 'closed for the week' and took a message.

units.author: courier
units.text: At Gilliver Village Hall, which opened as an information point this morning, a volunteer said about forty people had come in by lunchtime, 'mostly to ask if there's any news, and some to bring biscuits'. One man brought a set of marine charts of the Holm's east shore and left them on the table 'in case anybody needs them'.

units.title: Grieve exits island contract early
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Grieve Land Services has exited its Kittering Holm vegetation clearance contract, believed to be one of the largest single-site clearances in the region this year, before the work was complete. The client, Ardent Vale Holdings, is not known to have issued a replacement tender or appointed another contractor.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Contractors spoken to by the Journal said a 30-day programme at that scale was 'aggressive but not impossible' with the right crew numbers and plant. One said the industry 'will want to know how demobilisation was handled', given reports that workers remain on site. Grieve declined to comment beyond its statement.

units.title: Coastguard: daylight transfer being planned for the Holm
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 13:00 ST. At a short briefing in Port Ammet, a Coastguard officer said a daylight transfer from Kittering Holm is being planned 'with the vessels we actually have'. She said the island's dock was built for a landing barge, the forecast swell rules out a small-boat landing for at least two days, and the region's all-weather lifeboat is out of service for repair.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 13:20 ST. Asked whether a helicopter could be used, the officer said the island has no landing site that could be safely prepared and the aircraft is shared across three regions. Asked how many people are on the Holm, she said: 'We know someone activated a beacon. I'm not going to guess past that.'

units.title: Your Lyle Mutual policy: a quick reminder
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Dear policyholder, this is a reminder that your Lyle Mutual personal accident policy (ref. LM-PA-40217) remains active. Did you know your policy may not cover work at remote sites unless declared? Peace of mind is one call away. To update your details, visit your online account. Lyle Mutual: here for the long run. Terms and exclusions apply; see section 7(c).

units.title: Your remote site, your way!
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Hi there! Thinking about the season ahead? Our bestselling storm lantern is back in stock, with a 40-hour burn on one fill. Plus: our guide to keeping morale high at remote sites (spoiler: hot drinks and a good playlist). Mainland delivery in two to three days. Island and remote deliveries are temporarily unavailable, sorry! Stay cosy, the Camp Supply team

units.title: People are asking me
units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello. I'm sorry to write again when I know you can't reply. Since yesterday a lot of people have contacted the paper asking me whether the crew on the Holm are still there. I don't know, and I've told them so. 1) I have asked Grieve how many people were on site at the end of the contract. 2) I have asked Ardent Vale the same. 3) I have asked the Coastguard what they are planning. I'll print what I can stand up and nothing I can't. Nell Ashdown

units.title: rang them
units.author: sam
units.text: I rang the Coastguard. a very kind woman who sounded about nineteen said they know someone's out there and they're 'planning with the boats they have', and that she couldn't tell me who. I said I'm family and she said she understood and she still couldn't. I wasn't calm in the end. anyway. I've told Mum. she said 'they'll have a fire going', which is a very Mum thing to say. love, S x

units.title: Is he sleeping?
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Sorry. I keep thinking about how he never sleeps when he's worried, even at home, he gets up and tidies the cupboards. Is he sleeping? You don't have to answer that, I know you can't. A reporter from the Weyhaven paper rang me at work and I said I didn't want my name in it. If Tomas is there, tell him I'm fine and I'm being sensible. Ana

units.title: 'Our Gilliver Correspondent', February 1895: the camp men
units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: The men of the Holm timber camp came over on Tuesday last in two boats, a fortnight earlier than was looked for, and in poor spirits, for which the hard weather is no doubt to blame. Some went straight to the Ammet coach without taking a dinner. Mr Coad the agent tells your correspondent the camp is merely 'stood down for the frost'. It is said in the village that fewer came back than went, though your correspondent has counted none of them himself.

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project (1976): the window lamp
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Why did your family keep a lamp in the window? Mrs J. (b. 1899): 'For the boats, love. So the boats coming in could see the houses.' [pause] 'Well, the boats had the harbour light for that, I suppose.' [pause] 'My father said it was so they knew the house was awake. I never asked who they was. You didn't.'

units.title: LBC-0412: Gilliver shore, night ambience (1988)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue no. LBC-0412. Date: winter 1988 (cassette label). Location: Gilliver front, facing the Holm. Kit: mono cassette recorder, unknown mic. Duration 41 min. Content: harbour slap, a generator on a moored boat, gulls, two people talking about the price of diesel. At 33:10 one says 'they've a fire on the Holm' and the other says 'no they haven't'. Curator's note: no further information.

units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Day eight. Walked the whole east shore at low water. Oystercatcher, curlew, a single grey wagtail at the burn mouth. Browse heavy everywhere and still nothing has eaten it; were I a deer I should think it paradise. Boatman Creed would not come ashore to fetch the plant press. He held the boat off the rocks and shouted for me to hurry, though it was only two in the afternoon.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Decr. 16th. Snow in the night. 19 trees. The boat did not come, the sea being too high off the Gilliver side, and Coad says it will come when it comes. Roll called at dusk, 20 men. Lamps doubled on the yard. I have moved my ledger and my bunk into the store hut nearer the fire, the clerk's hut being cold and standing alone.

units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Dec. 12. Blowing hard S.E., no going out. Mended pots in the shed all day with Jory. Fish 1s 2d the stone at the quay, which is robbery. Mother had the lamp lit before four and wouldnt have it moved from the window for the draught. Jory asked her who it was for and she said 'for manners' and give him a clip for asking.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Jan. 19. 00:00 wind SE 5, rain, vis. moderate. 01:30 lamp burning well. 02:45 wind SE 6, rain heavy. Remarks: walkers on the shore road again, three this time, standing below the stile. Did not answer when hailed from the door. Rain too heavy to make out coats. Rowe asks that this be entered 'as seen by both keepers'. Entered. E.S.

units.title: Was that a helicopter over the Holm this morning?
units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Was doing an early job on the Gilliver road and something low and noisy went out over the water towards the Holm about half six, then came back. My cousin says it was the rescue helicopter and it didn't land. I didn't see it land either but I was up a ladder with a hedge trimmer at the time so I'm no witness.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Davey, I logged it from the station: a twin-engine fixed-wing aircraft, not a helicopter, east to west at about 300 metres, 06:34 and again 06:51. The wind farm survey contractor has been flying that pattern off the point all autumn; it's in my notes from three weeks ago. Sorry to be the dull answer, but it's the right one.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: The Coastguard say 'we know someone activated a beacon'. Someone. Not 'the crew'. Why that word? I've had three emails on my list from people saying the workers were taken off days ago and the beacon is automatic. I'm not saying that's true. I'm asking why nobody will say how many.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Because, Gil, the Coastguard can't count people over a radio. 'Someone' is the honest word. Also, beacons of that type don't go off by themselves late at night and then get acknowledged. Your list is telling you two opposite things in one week: they were abandoned on purpose, and they were never there. Both can't be true.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: I never said abandoned 'on purpose', go back and read it. I said the crew weren't part of the plan, which is different. And I'm allowed to share what people send me. That's what a mailing list is for. People can make up their own minds.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Helicopter. Job done. Why is everyone making this so complicated. There's a whole helicopter sitting at Weyhaven doing nothing most days, I've seen it from the bypass.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Cal, the Coastguard answered that at their briefing an hour ago, and Sound FM has it on its page, linked here. There is no landing site and the aircraft is shared across three regions. Please read the thread before posting. Pell.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Finding 1, for what it's worth: the intermediary that bought the Holm for Ardent Vale also filed the dock works notice, not Grieve. So if anyone has a duty regarding the dock, on paper, it's the owner. Finding 2 I'm not posting until I've checked it twice. I was wrong about two properties last week and I've apologised for that.

units.title: Rescue planning: what has actually been said.
units.author: sb_mod
units.text: To keep the main thread readable, this one is for official statements only, quoted with a link. So far: the Coastguard notices (two), Sound Lines' bulletin on its relief vessel, the council's information point at Gilliver Hall, and Grieve's statement. If you post a rumour here I will move it. If it turns out to be true I'll apologise and move it back. Pell.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Fair dos, that's me told. Cousin's been told too. Should have known, he also told me Pebble the cat had turned up in a shed in Tollinby, when everyone on here knows she was in Port Ammet the whole time.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: For the list, Sound Lines today: relief vessel 'completing a refit at Weyhaven and is not yet in service', 'no sailing has been scheduled'. From the boat tonight: the afternoon sailing ran forty minutes late because of the swell at Lisle. If they can't keep the Lisle run to time in this, nobody is landing on the Holm tomorrow.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: She was in Mr Garside's shed on Quay Lane, two doors down, thank you Davey! Pebble (grey, one white sock) is very well and still won't go out once it's dark, which this week I'm not arguing with. I've left the hall light on all night for her. Thinking of the families, and thank you everyone who asked after her.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Today: pressure falling, 1021 to 1009 hPa since breakfast, which is quick. Wind SW 16 knots gusting 31 by six. Swell at the point already 1.8 m on a long period, and that's what makes the Holm dock nasty, not the wind sea. Rain arrived 17:40. Expect a rough night and a rougher tomorrow. Overnight minimum pressure in the morning.

units.title: Relief boat refit, for anyone asking
units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: For anyone asking where the relief boat is: on the slip at Weyhaven, gearbox in, shaft alignment done this morning, antifouling drying. Earliest she floats is tomorrow, and with a gale forecast the yard won't let her out of the basin. I've asked for floodlights on the foredeck and a second landing ladder. Management said yes to both, which I'm writing down.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: What I want to know is who's doing the landing assessment. The Holm dock is Grieve's barge ramp and a wooden pier. Nobody on our side has stood on it. If the boards are rotten or the ramp's underwater at half tide, that's a different plan, and I'd like to know before I'm stood on the bow with a line.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: Good lad Seth. Lads, chandlery has landing lines, fenders and two new boarding ladders if the company wants them, cost price, I've told them. Nobody's paying me for that so don't start. And no, I'm not coming on the boat, I get sick on the Lisle run.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Pier's sound, or was a fortnight back when I passed close. The ramp dries at half tide on springs, and it's springs end of the week. Somebody should tell them that properly. I told the Coastguard lass on the phone but I don't know if it got written down.

units.title: Lisle slip tonight
units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Not working the slip now, I'm on days at the bakery... but I walked down after tea. The Lisle side has lamps in windows too, which it never did, that was always a Gilliver thing... ha, anyway. The night boat came in on time despite the swell. Kerris waved. I didn't wave back fast enough and felt silly.

units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: That's a good thing you did with the tray. Out here we'd call that van a sleeper, somebody run out of hours and too tired to start the heater, lying down across the seats where you can't see them. I've been that van. Coffee, a stretch, a lit lot. Rolling west tonight, mostly wheat and wind. Ten-four.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Merle, that's kind and probably right. Tonight's van had a man in it, asleep with his hat over his face, and I've never been so pleased to see a hat. Sourdough rose like a dream. Puns to follow when I've slept, or maybe I'll just loaf about.

units.title: Patrol log, east gate
units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: 01:20 patrol east gate to row K. Reefer units humming, nil found. 01:40 monitor 4 showed the figure at the edge of the lot again, by the light pole at the fence. Walked out with the torch. Fox, sitting. It looked at me like I owed it money. Logged as fox. 02:05 tea.

units.title: Retail park, slow night
units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Slow night at the retail park. Control rang at half twelve to ask if I'd seen 'the van', meaning my van from weeks ago. I hadn't. Control then spent ten minutes telling me how he'd go and get those island lads himself if it wasn't for the swell. Control doesn't own a boat. Patrol, nil found.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Orla, I was one of the eleven, I think. I didn't get through, which is just as well; I only wanted to say that the bookshop is staying open late this week in case anyone in Tollinby can't sit at home with the radio. There's a kettle and the poetry shelf. That's all I had. Gently, everyone.

units.title: Quiet house tonight
units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: Quiet house tonight. Mrs A. asks for the blind up so she can see the yard light, and we sit with it for a while. The intercom has been quiet since the electrician, and I find I listen for it anyway at ten past three. Hot chocolate round at four. Sorry this is short, the night bell's going.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Clinical note, since people keep asking me privately: if you have family in a situation like this, you will not sleep properly, and that is a normal response, not a failing. Short naps, daylight in the morning, eat something. And please don't spend the night refreshing a forum. n of 1, but I've watched it make people worse.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: home from the depot at five love and the night drivers had the radio on in the canteen all shift and every time the island came on everyone went quiet even Pete who never stops, I'll keep my mouth shut on the landing don't worry, and the stairwell was fine this morning it was light by the time I came up

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, I agree with Bev. When my late husband's ship was overdue in the winter of 1979, the worst of it was the people who meant well. I have written a card for the young woman's friend on 4 and left it with Hassan, to pass on only if it is wanted. The stairwell is still lit, and I still use the lift. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Card from Irena received and kept behind the till. Also: I have the big lantern batteries back in, cost price, and the bread van is on time this week for once. If the lady on 4 wants anything carried up, or nothing at all, she knows where I am. H

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: A lovely recording, thank you. On my old machine the thrush would have been lost in the hiss, which I'd have enjoyed just as much. It is good to hear the reservoir sounding ordinary, and I was glad to see your name back on the board. Regards, Ned

units.title: Please do not go 'listening for the Holm'
units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Moderator note. A few members have asked about taking dishes or hydrophones to Gilliver to 'listen for the Holm'. Please don't. Real people are waiting for a real rescue, and their families may well find this forum. LowBand is for recordings, not stories, and certainly not for turning a search into content. Threads that try will be locked.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Agree. Practical note for anyone tempted: at nine kilometres in a gale you'd record your own boat, the harbour pump and a generator on somebody's trawler. I know because I've tried it on calm nights as a hobby. You will not hear a camp. Stay home, keep your kit dry.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: guys im literally going to Gilliver tomorrow night with the big parabolic, we are going LIVE from the harbour wall, can we hear the island?? insane. link in bio, drop a sub, this is history and nobody else is brave enough to do it

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Removed a post above for exactly the reason stated in the first post. NightScreamLive, you were temp-banned before for re-uploading other people's files; this is your last warning. Thread locked. If anyone has a normal recording to share, start a normal thread.
